title: Matsya's boat and the end of an age
word: the ten avatars as a series
hook: a boat of seeds and sages, and a neighbor's ark
carry: pralaya: an age ends, the seeds and sages go on
tomorrow: someone steals the Vedas while Brahma sleeps. who goes after them?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Matsya: a fingertip fish carried from jar to sea, because the Lord can come as the smallest creature. Today, the flood it warned of, and what goes in the boat.

Ask people what they'd grab if they had to leave home fast, and the answers are a passport, a photo album, a grandmother's ring. The fish gives Manu his own list. Build a boat. Gather the seeds of all that grows. Take the sages with you. When the water comes, the fish says, I'll come, and you'll know me by my horn. Then the rain doesn't stop, and the sea climbs over the land.
screen: `WHAT WOULD YOU GRAB?` → `SEEDS. SAGES. A BOAT.` → `THE SEA CLIMBS OVER THE LAND.`

segments.voice: It happens as the fish said. The boat floats, the horned fish appears, and Manu ties the boat to it with a great serpent for a rope. The fish pulls them through the flood, answering Manu's questions as they go; the Matsya Purana presents itself as that teaching. This flood has a name in Hindu teaching: pralaya, the dissolving of the world at the end of an age. In the Bhagavata's telling it comes as Brahma's day ends and he sleeps. Hindu time turns in cycles; worlds dissolve and begin again. So, who gets to start the world again? The answer is in the boat: seeds so things can grow, sages so wisdom isn't lost, and one person who was kind to something small. In an older telling, the Shatapatha Brahmana, people come from Manu after the waters go down. A neighbor knows a story like this. In Genesis, a book Jews and Christians both keep, Noah is told to bring living things into the ark, "to keep them alive with thee." And of Noah's sons the text says: "and of them was the whole earth overspread." Here's what the two share: one boat kept through the water, and everyone after it in one family. And one honest difference. Genesis gives a reason, saying "the earth was filled with violence," and it ends with a promise, a bow in the cloud, that such a flood won't come again. In Hindu time, the flood is one turn of a cycle, and what rides it out, with the seeds, is a teaching.
screen: `PRALAYA: AN AGE DISSOLVES.` · `SEEDS, SAGES, ONE KIND PERSON.` · `GENESIS: ONE BOAT, ONE FAMILY.` · then, large: `ONE DIFFERENCE: A PROMISE, OR A CYCLE.`

segments.voice: Count on your fingers, slowly, what you'd want carried through a hard season: a person, a skill, a few words someone gave you, a recipe. One finger for each, and a quiet thank-you for each one. If you pray, you can entrust them to God.
The ten avatars as a series: Matsya, the fish, pulls a boat of seeds and sages through the flood.

segments.voice: For the road: pralaya, an age ends, and the seeds and sages go on. Rest well.
